question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a GTK-native Linux companion as the canonical remaining implementation, and who will own its staged acceptance?
rationale: The roadmap supports a Linux companion, but no viable implementation PR remains and the proposed architectures create materially different dependency, packaging, security, and long-term maintenance commitments.

options.title: Sponsor Staged GTK App
options.body: Name a platform owner and approve a minimal native GTK milestone with explicit packaging, pairing, approval, lifecycle, security, and live-proof gates.

options.title: Choose Shared Desktop Shell
options.body: Sponsor a Tauri-style shared desktop architecture and explicitly accept its additional runtime and supply-chain model.

options.title: Defer Linux Companion
options.body: Continue supporting Linux through the stable Gateway and postpone a native companion until durable ownership is available.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Staged GTK App
recommendation.body: Name a platform owner and approve a minimal native GTK milestone with explicit packaging, pairing, approval, lifecycle, security, and live-proof gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion contains the strongest available product-direction signal and the explicit native Linux preference.
